data.gender_notes: Alake is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Alake was a name given to the goddesses of protection and the guardians of the gates to the underworld. The name Alake means 'ruler' or 'guardian', making it a fitting name for a boy who is expected to protect and lead. The name Alake carries the meaning “Ruler, Guardian” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alake usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, guardian and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alake total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Alake holds significant cultural impact even in Christianity. In the Christendom context, the name Alake can be linked to various Christian figures and their roles. One such influential figure is Alake Adekola II, a traditional ruler and the Orangbemi of Ile-Ife, Nigeria. He is an integral part of Nigerian Christianity and symbolizes cultural preservation, unity, and progress.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper, spiritual level, the name Alake signifies the person's role as a guardian of faith and morals, someone who shields and protects their community. Christians with the name Alake are guided by the divine power to uplift, lead, and inspire others in their walk with God. The name Alake represents a commitment to following and serving Christ as a steadfast ruler and protector for others.
